name: The Great North Road

layers.essential_history: [[c:The Great North Road from London to Scotland once ran right through Wansford. The village has since been bypassed, but the old road still runs through it.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:Coaching inns along the road changed horses and fed travellers on the long journey north.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:Signor Rossi's show wagon is here. He says he was performing all night: his ticket stubs prove it.]]

puzzle.title: [[c:The ticket stubs]]
material: [[c:SIGNOR ROSSI: "Three shows tonight, forty people at each. I tore every ticket myself."]]
[[c:You count the stubs: one hundred and twenty.]]
puzzle.question: [[c:Does Signor Rossi's story add up? (yes or no)]]
puzzle.reveal: [[c:Yes. Three shows of forty is 120, and there are 120 stubs. Signor Rossi was busy all night.]]
puzzle.fallback: [[c:Stuck? Take a hint: hints are free.]]

evidence: [[c:Signor Rossi was performing all night: his ticket stubs add up.]]
directions_to_next: [[c:Head south-east, about 410 metres as the crow flies, to the Papermills. Head back over to the south side of the river. Keep to pavements and public paths.]]
